description: Economic hypothesis library for strategy generation

logics.name: Funding Volatility Filter
logics.thesis: When funding rate volatility is low, carry risk is lower because funding is unlikely to flip negative. Enter only during low-vol windows.

logics.name: Funding Regime Contrarian
logics.thesis: Extreme funding rates signal crowding. When funding is in top percentiles, the position is crowded and reversal is likely. Take contrarian (short-perp) position.

logics.name: Funding Z-Score Dynamic Threshold
logics.thesis: Fixed-threshold strategies adapt poorly to regime changes. A z-score threshold adapts to changing funding distributions.

logics.name: Cross-Symbol Funding Spread
logics.thesis: When one symbol has much higher funding than another, go long the low-funding and short the high-funding symbol. Captures relative funding without market exposure.

logics.name: Funding-Price Divergence
logics.thesis: When funding is very positive but price is falling, longs are paying high funding while price is against them. Forced exits may follow. Contrarian signal.

logics.name: Weekend Funding Effect
logics.thesis: Weekend funding behavior differs due to lower liquidity. Test if funding carry has different weekend vs weekday characteristics.

logics.name: Short-Term Mean Reversion
logics.thesis: Keltner captures medium-term (14-period) mean reversion. Test shorter windows (5-7 periods) to capture intraday/weekly reversal.

logics.name: Volatility Regime Transition
logics.thesis: When volatility shifts from low to high regime, prices often over-react. Trade the initial over-reaction.

logics.name: End-of-Month Rebalancing
logics.thesis: Institutional rebalancing happens at month-end. Prices may drift in predictable directions on the last 2-3 days of each month.

logics.name: Funding Mean Reversion
logics.thesis: Funding rates mean-revert to a long-term average. When funding deviates, entering a carry position captures both the rate and reversion premium.
